claim_text: [NEGATIVE RESULT] In the replicated bounded matrix (4 size distributions x 2 layouts x 3 seeds, n=320), the declared median/90th-percentile two-tier policy emitted more unique candidate pairs than the minimum over the predeclared single-tier grid for every one of 24 identical scenes; paired differences ranged from +4 to +1413 in both runs.
confounds: Only n=320 was run; larger object counts and other domains were not tested.
The fixed-grid oracle is selected after evaluating the declared grid, so this is not a comparison to one preselected cell size.
Only the implemented assignment/query policy was tested.

claim_text: [NEGATIVE RESULT] In both runs, the two-tier policy failed to reduce candidate pairs in mono-size, low-dispersion lognormal, separated bimodal, and truncated Pareto-like conditions under both uniform and clustered layouts; clustered scenes had larger median positive paired differences than uniform scenes for each distribution.
confounds: The layout comparison changes realized overlap counts and occupancy, so the observed magnitude difference is not an isolated density causal effect.
Only one clustered-center parameterization and one domain size were used.
Three seeds provide a finite deterministic sample, not population-level uncertainty.

claim_text: [UNSUPPORTED EXTRAPOLATION] The replicated matrix does not establish the proposed low-dispersion crossover or a bimodal advantage: the sign never changed in the tested sequence because all observed paired differences were positive. It cannot establish that no crossover exists outside the tested distributions, n, domain, grid, or policy.
confounds: No intermediate dispersion sweep was run between loglow and bimodal.
No sensitivity policy was run to separate percentile choice from assignment/query policy.
The experiment does not cover anisotropic AABBs or other spatial structures.

claim_text: [METHOD CHECK] For all 265 result rows in each run, including the extra permutation row, the number of true overlaps among generated candidates equaled the all-pairs true-overlap count; the tested implementations therefore produced no observed false negatives under the declared AABB and boundary conventions.
confounds: This is an empirical check of these finite scenes, not a proof for arbitrary inputs.
The all-pairs oracle uses the same AABB representation and overlap convention as candidate evaluation.
Hash correctness was not independently reimplemented.

claim_text: [METHOD CHECK] Single-tier and two-tier candidates were globally deduplicated as unordered object-ID pairs and used the same inclusive-maximum/floor cell convention; the recorded comparisons therefore do not show an unequal pair-deduplication or boundary-rule confound.
confounds: Boundary behavior was not stress-tested with objects exactly on cell boundaries.
The two-tier method intentionally changes tier assignment and cross-tier querying, so equal boundary rules do not make the algorithms otherwise identical.
The implementation stores integer-index pairs, but overflow limits were not stress-tested.

claim_text: [LIMITATION] The tested adaptive method is not solely a test of median and 90th-percentile scale selection: objects at or below the median are inserted in the small hash, larger objects in the large hash, same-tier pairs are queried within tier, and cross-tier pairs query large objects against the small-object hash. Any measured difference is attributable to this complete policy, not percentile statistics in isolation.
confounds: No both-tier insertion variant or alternative cross-tier query policy was executed.
Hierarchical/multiscale spatial hashing is prior art, so this implementation must not be generalized to all hierarchical hashes.

claim_text: [METHOD CHECK] One clustered bimodal fixture with a declared ID/insertion permutation produced the same two-tier unique candidate count (1861) before and after permutation in both runs; this supports order invariance for that fixture and policy only.
confounds: Only one condition, seed, permutation, and method was checked.
The permuted scene hash necessarily changed because object order/IDs changed; count equality, not hash equality, is the relevant check.
Single-tier order invariance was not separately recorded.

claim_text: [LIMITATION] Candidate-pair counts alone do not support claims about wall-clock time, memory, cache behavior, insertion/query cost, or narrow-phase accuracy. The run records cell-visit counters and elapsed timings but the notebook explicitly treats those as secondary and does not provide a controlled performance comparison.
confounds: Python timing is not a controlled systems benchmark.
The two-tier policy can trade candidate count against cell visits and storage, which was not analyzed as a primary outcome.

claim_text: [LIMITATION] The bounded run does not satisfy the full planned factorial design: it uses one object count, cube-only AABBs, two spatial layouts, no explicit sparse/crowded matched controls, and no anisotropic or domain-size sensitivity. Conclusions must therefore remain restricted to the recorded n=320 cube scenes in a 100^3 domain.
confounds: Realized occupancy and overlap counts differ across generated conditions.
The bounded cap was chosen for local execution and does not replace the omitted factors.

claim_text: [LIMITATION] The result cannot be presented as evidence that adaptive or hierarchical spatial hashing is novel or generally ineffective: mapped primary sources already describe adaptive subdivision, hierarchical hashing, and size/grid-resolution adaptations. The only empirical claim available here concerns this specified median/90th policy and protocol.
confounds: The mapped studies use different primitives, workloads, and objectives; they do not validate or invalidate this exact AABB count comparison.
Replication of the exact protocol does not establish novelty for the broader adaptive/hierarchical method family.
